name: Ha'amonga 'a Maui
note: Archaeological monument: a coral-limestone trilithon near Niutoua in the north-east, Tongatapu's best-known landmark.

name: Ancient Royal Tombs of Lapaha
note: Archaeological site: terraced langi (royal tombs) of the Tuʻi Tonga kings, near Mu'a, with information signs. Wikipedia title redirects to Muʻa (town), so views count 0.

name: Mu'a
note: Village and former capital on the lagoon's east edge, with the langi royal tombs and the Paepaʻo Teleʻa tombs.

name: Mapu 'a Vaea
note: Natural feature: coral-reef blowholes near Houma on the south-west coast, best viewed at high tide.

name: Hufangalupe
note: Natural feature: a limestone land bridge over a sinkhole on the south-east coast, with viewpoints around the crater.

name: Nukuʻalofa
note: Town: Tonga's capital on the north coast, with the waterfront, markets, churches and most of the island's accommodation.

name: Royal Palace
note: Building: the crumbling 1867 wooden royal residence in Nukuʻalofa; grounds closed to visitors, so seen from outside.

name: Talamahu Market
note: Market: the main daily produce and handicraft market hall in Nukuʻalofa, with carvings, tapa and jewellery upstairs.

name: Tonga National Museum
note: Museum in Nukuʻalofa with historic artefacts, including the preserved shell of the tortoise Tuʻi Malila.

name: Tukuʻaho Memorial Museum
note: Museum: small history museum of royal artefacts and Polynesian education history, open by appointment.

name: Captain Cook Landing Site
note: Historic landmark: where Captain James Cook first reached land in Tonga, along Taufaʻahau Road between Holonga and Alaki.

name: Abel Tasman Landing Site
note: Historic landmark: the first European landing in Tonga (Abel Tasman, over a century before Cook), at the end of Hihifo Road, Haʻatafu.

name: Haʻatafu Beach
note: Beach: long white-sand beach with palms and coral on the north-western peninsula, good for snorkelling and sunsets.

name: Matatahi 'Anahulu Beach
note: Beach: sandy beach within walking distance of the Anahulu Caves, south-east of the island.

name: Anahulu Caves
note: Natural attraction: partly flooded limestone caves with freshwater pools; guided tours, with optional swimming.

name: Niutao Beach
note: Beach: small beach on the north coast, free to visit, with little on site. Wikivoyage gives only a 3-decimal point: needs OSM.

name: Pangaimotu Island
note: Island: small resort island off Nukuʻalofa with a sunken wreck to snorkel, a restaurant and gear hire, reached by boat.

name: Fafa Island
note: Island: small resort island reached by ferry from Nukuʻalofa for a day trip or overnight stay.

name: ʻAtata Island
note: Island: small island off Tongatapu's north coast, a resort day trip or overnight stay by ferry.

name: Flying Fox Reserve
note: Wildlife reserve: flying fox (fruit bat) colony in Kolovai village on the western side of the island. No reserve point found: Kolovai village page point not used.

name: Hule Fortress
note: Historic site: an old fortress earthwork at Nukunuku in the western district; no visitor source found describing a visit.

name: Nukuleka
note: Archaeological site: possibly the first Lapita settlement in Tonga, on the east coast; no visitor source found.

name: Malaʻe Kula
note: Cemetery: Nukuʻalofa's cemetery, where the ornate royal family tomb is the main sight.

name: Centenary Church
note: Church: Polynesian-style Methodist church in Nukuʻalofa, attended by the royal family at Easter; seen mainly from outside.

name: Nukuʻalofa Cathedral
note: Church ruin: baroque-facade cathedral of the Free Church of Tonga, damaged by Cyclone Gita; entry not permitted.

name: Basilica of St Anthony of Padua
wiki: Basilica of St. Anthony of Padua, Nukuʻalofa
note: Church: contemporary basilica in Nukuʻalofa with a pagoda-like design drawn from traditional Polynesian architecture.

name: St Mary's Cathedral
note: Church: seat of the Catholic diocese of Tonga, with two low baroque towers flanking a modern nave on Vuna Road.

name: Tongan War Memorial
note: Memorial: small cenotaph in Nukuʻalofa for Tongans who died in the First and Second World Wars.

name: Ancient Tonga
note: Cultural centre: Tongan buffet with traditional dance show, held on Fridays (pre-booking), on Tamakautonga Road in Nukuʻalofa.

name: Oholei Beach Dinner and Show
note: Cultural venue: Tongan dinner and traditional show held inside Hina cave on the beach near the airport, booked through the visitor centre.
